title: Decoding run dichotomy
statement: Let $a,b,f,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x,\beta,y$ be Boolean words. Suppose $y$ is the pair encoding of $x$ and $\beta$, and let $st$ be a register record whose fifteen entries are at most $B$. Assume that the query-length register of $st$ equals $|y|$, its pair-scan pointer is $2|x|+2$, its width-check pointer equals that pair-scan pointer, its index and decoding scratch registers are zero, and its width cap $k$ satisfies $1\le k$ and $2k\le B$. Then either $|\beta|\le |\mathrm{bits}(k)|$ and $\beta$ is canonical, in which case there exist $q',k'\le B$ such that the machine $A(a,b,f,m)$ with the oracle determined by $N$ reaches the label for the $2n\le i$ comparison from the state labeled by the true width-check test, with register values $st$ and no result recorded, while satisfying its guard at every earlier time; the final register values are those of $st$ with the query-length register set to the pair-scan pointer, the index set to the binary value of $\beta$, and the width-check pointer and cap set to $q'$ and $k'$. Or the conjunction of that length bound and canonicity fails, and the same initial configuration halts with result false while satisfying its guard at every earlier time.

Let $a,b,f,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the
Boolean alphabet, let $x,\beta,y$ be Boolean words, and let $\mathrm{mode}$ be a
Boolean. Suppose $y$ is the pair encoding of $x$ and $\beta$, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a
register record whose fifteen entries are all at most $B$. Assume its query pointer
equals $|y|$, its pair-scan pointer equals $2|x|+2$, its width-check pointer equals its
pair-scan pointer, its index and decoding scratch are zero, and its width cap $k$
satisfies $1\le k$ and $2k\le B$. Then either $\beta$ has length at most the length of
the binary expansion of $k$ and is canonical (every nonempty canonical word ends in
true), in which case there are $q',k'\le B$ such that the register machine $A$ with
oracle determined by $N$ reaches the decoding-comparison label from the initial label
and registers $\mathrm{st}$, with no answer recorded, while satisfying its guard
throughout; the final registers are obtained from $\mathrm{st}$ by setting the query
pointer to the pair-scan pointer, the index to the value of $\beta$, and the width-check
pointer and cap to $q'$ and $k'$. Or that length bound and canonicity condition fails,
and the machine halts with answer false from the same initial configuration while
satisfying the guard throughout.
